reservation_method: None — no wilderness permit is issued for this area.
notes: Day hikers to non-wilderness peaks generally need nothing else.

reservation_method: For each quota'd trailhead, 50% of the quota is reservable on recreation.gov starting 6 months before entry (printable up to 7 days before entry); the remaining 50% opens 3 days before entry, printable immediately. Online purchase only -- no phone or in-person reservations. Trip leader must carry a signed physical (printed) copy for the whole trip.
fee_notes: $8/person ages 13+ (12 and under free) plus $6 non-refundable service fee per permit; recreation fee refundable only if cancelled 14+ days before entry
notes: Quota'd trailheads on the Humboldt-Toiyabe (Bridgeport RD) portion only: Buckeye Creek, Green Creek, Horse Creek, Leavitt Meadows, Little Slide Canyon, Robinson Creek (the trail out of Twin Lakes/Mono Village), and Virginia Lakes. A permit is required year-round for overnight stays even outside the Jun 15 - Oct 15 quota window, but the source does not state the off-season issuance method -- call the Bridgeport Ranger District (760-932-7070, Mon-Fri 8:30am-4pm PST) rather than assuming free self-issue.
interagency_note: Confirmed: a Hoover Wilderness permit is honored for continuous travel into Yosemite National Park, Inyo National Forest, or Stanislaus National Forest without a separate permit -- 'with exceptions' per the source (e.g. the stricter 8-person/no-stock Sawtooth Ridge Zone cap still applies, and each area's own group-size/food-storage/campfire rules must still be followed). Applies e.g. to Twin Lakes via Robinson Creek/Peeler Lake/Rock Island Pass into Kerrick Canyon for Tower Peak.

permit_type: Inyo NF Wilderness Permit (John Muir / Ansel Adams / Golden Trout-Inyo / Hoover-Inyo entries)
reservation_method: 60% of each trailhead's daily quota reservable on recreation.gov starting 6 months (7am Pacific) before entry; remaining 40% released 2 weeks before entry, same release time. Reservations can be made up to the day of the trip if quota space remains; cancelled permits return space to the calendar within 24 hours.
fee_notes: $6/permit + $5/person ($15/person if the trip enters or exits via the Mt. Whitney Zone)
notes: Inyo NF issues permits for the John Muir, Ansel Adams, Hoover and Golden Trout Wildernesses, so it administers part of Hoover alongside Humboldt-Toiyabe NF. Popular trailheads (Kearsarge Pass, Bishop Pass, Rush Creek, Cottonwood) can sell out within minutes of release. Outside May 1 - Nov 1 permits are free/self-issue, no reservation needed.
interagency_note: Honored for continuous travel into neighboring parks: Yosemite NP (Tioga Pass, Saddlebag Lake, Virginia Lakes, Walker Lake/Bloody Canyon corridors) and Sequoia & Kings Canyon NP (Taboose, Sawmill, Baxter, Shepherd Pass, Kearsarge Pass, Cottonwood Pass corridors) — no separate NPS permit needed. Per the official page: this requires *continuous* wilderness travel: a break (exiting to town and re-entering elsewhere) requires a new permit from the agency where the next section starts, except a reasonable resupply break for long-distance through-hikers.

permit_type: Inyo NF Wilderness Permit (Hoover Wilderness portion -- non-quota)
reservation_method: Non-quota -- not part of the 6-month/2-week rolling reservation system. Presumed free self-issue at trailhead or ranger station kiosk, consistent with every other 'Non Quota--Unlimited'-labeled trail on Inyo NF's own table (e.g. Kennedy Meadows South, Trail Pass, Wildrose); NOT explicitly restated for this specific trail, so treat as an inference from the pattern rather than a direct quote.
fee_notes: Free (assumed, matching the self-issue pattern for other Inyo NF non-quota trails -- not explicitly confirmed for this trail)
notes: Lundy Canyon (trail code HH01) and Saddlebag Lake (HH04) are both Inyo NF-administered (HH = Hoover Wilderness) and non-quota. Both were previously mis-tagged here -- Lundy Canyon to Humboldt-Toiyabe's quota'd hoover group, Saddlebag Lake to the quota'd inyo_jmw_aaw group. The agency and quota-status facts are unlikely to have changed, but this is the oldest source in the dataset, so re-confirm before a real trip.
interagency_note: Same continuous-travel reciprocity into Yosemite/Ansel Adams as the general Inyo NF permit.
excludes: Commercial guiding in this portion of Hoover Wilderness is restricted to Yosemite Mountain Guides; a wilderness permit does not authorise guided trips by anyone else. Relevant only to commercial parties.

permit_type: Mount Whitney Zone Permit (classic Mt. Whitney Trail only -- see notes)
reservation_method: Lottery on recreation.gov: apply Feb 1 - Mar 1, results published Mar 15, claim & pay the $15/person fee by Apr 21. Unclaimed dates open first-come at 7am Pacific on Apr 22. Outside the quota season (Nov 2 - Apr 30), permits are still required and still reserved online (not walk-up self-issue) but are unlimited -- reservable up to 2 weeks ahead.
fee_notes: $15/person lottery-claim/reservation fee; a $6 recreation.gov service fee applies as with other permits on this system (not explicitly restated on this page)
notes: One results date only: March 15. Daily quota is 100 people/day for Day Use permits and 60 people/day for Overnight permits. Day Use permits are valid one day only (midnight to midnight), cannot be consecutive, and cannot be combined with other permits to pass through or exit the zone.
interagency_note: For the OVERNIGHT Mt. Whitney Trail permit only (not Day Use): can extend for multiple nights and exit via the John Muir Trail into Yosemite National Park without a separate permit. Day Use permits explicitly cannot be combined with other permits for pass-through/exit.
excludes: Covers the classic Mt. Whitney Trail ONLY -- Day Use or Overnight, for objectives like Mount Whitney itself and Mount Muir. It does NOT cover climbs approaching via the North Fork of Lone Pine Creek trail: the Mountaineers Route, East Face, East Buttress, or Mount Russell. Those use an ordinary Inyo NF wilderness permit instead (permit_group inyo_jmw_aaw), which is a different product with a different release mechanism, so you cannot enter the lottery and expect to be covered. MODELLING CAVEAT: this project tags the whole Whitney Portal trailhead to whitney_zone uniformly and holds no route-level data, so any peak reached by that different approach may be mismodelled here. Verify your actual route before relying on the permit type shown.

permit_type: Inyo NF Wilderness Permit (Golden Trout Wilderness portion -- Cottonwood Basin/Cottonwood Pass)
reservation_method: Same recreation.gov mechanics as the general Inyo NF permit: 60% of quota reservable starting 6 months before entry, remaining 40% released 2 weeks before entry. Select the Cottonwood Lakes (trail code GT39) or Cottonwood Pass (GT60) trail specifically, NOT a John Muir/Ansel Adams trail.
fee_notes: $6/permit + $5/person (same fee structure as the general Inyo NF permit; not independently reconfirmed for this trail specifically)
notes: GT-coded trails (trail code begins with GT) run the last Friday in June through September 15, not the general May 1 - Nov 1 Inyo season: Cottonwood Lakes (GT39, quota 60/day, 36/24 split) and Cottonwood Pass (GT60, quota 40/day, 24/16 split). recreation.gov's summary calendar disagrees, naming a May 1 - Nov 1 season for Cottonwood Pass; it is treated as the outlier. Outside the quota season a permit is still required, free/self-issue, but obtained from Inyo NF for this entry rather than Sequoia NF.
interagency_note: Same reciprocity as the general Inyo NF permit: honored for continuous travel into neighboring Golden Trout Wilderness (Sequoia NF side, self-issue) and onward per the same continuous-travel condition.

permit_type: Sierra NF Wilderness Permit (John Muir / Ansel Adams west side, Dinkey Lakes, Kaiser)
reservation_method: Quotas apply year-round (no off-season exemption). 60% of the trailhead quota reservable on recreation.gov in a continuous rolling window from 6 months up to 14 days before entry (bookable until 1 day before if space remains); the other 40% is also on recreation.gov, released for shorter-notice/walk-up booking. No phone reservations. Permit must be picked up in person at the High Sierra or Bass Lake Ranger District by 10am the day of entry, unless prior arrangements are made.
notes: Permits and quotas are required year-round for overnight trips into the John Muir, Ansel Adams, Dinkey Lakes and Kaiser Wildernesses; day hikes need no permit.
interagency_note: Honored for continuous travel into Yosemite National Park via Isberg Pass (e.g. Clover Meadow/Isberg trailhead to Foerster Peak) or into Sequoia/Kings Canyon — no separate NPS permit needed, but per the official page the National Park must be listed on your itinerary when you reserve for the interagency permit to be honored there. Conversely, a National Park permit is valid on this forest's wilderness only if it's listed on that itinerary too.

reservation_method: 60% of each week's quota is allocated by a WEEKLY LOTTERY, not simple first-come booking: for each week-long hiking-start window, the lottery application period opens Sunday 12:01am and closes the following Saturday 11:59pm, roughly 24 weeks (168 days) before that week, with results notified by Monday 5pm. Lottery-unclaimed spots from that week open first-come-first-served on recreation.gov the Friday after the application period closes, up to 3 days before entry. The remaining 40% of each week's quota becomes available on recreation.gov 7 days in advance (up to 3 days before entry), first-come.
fee_notes: $5/person reservation fee (not independently reconfirmed this pass)
notes: The 60% portion is a weekly lottery cycle rather than a rolling reservation window -- structurally closer to the Whitney Zone lottery than to Inyo's system, on a weekly rather than annual cadence. Season start is NOT a fixed May 1 park-wide: reservations open for late-April start dates in some but not all areas of the park, with per-area dates in a dataset linked from the source page that has not been retrieved here, so treat 05-01 as an approximation. Off-season permits are free, self-issue, no quota. Current window: https://www.nps.gov/yose/planyourvisit/wildpermitdates.htm
interagency_note: Yosemite-issued permits are likewise honored if your route continues out into neighboring Inyo, Sierra, Stanislaus or Humboldt-Toiyabe NF wilderness on the same continuous trip.

reservation_method: Confirmed genuinely a simple rolling release, not a lottery (unlike Yosemite): reservations open on recreation.gov up to 6 months before entry, released daily at 7:00am Pacific. Entry point and entry date cannot be changed after booking (would need a new reservation); exit date/itinerary can be adjusted later. Permit must be PHYSICALLY PICKED UP at the trailhead's Wilderness Office/desk -- a recreation.gov confirmation email is not a valid permit. Pickup window: as early as 1pm the day before entry, no later than 10am the morning of entry; call ahead (559-565-3766) if you'll be later or the reservation is cancelled at 10am and released to walk-ups.
fee_notes: $15/trip + $5/person within quota season; per-person portion refundable if cancelled up to 1 week before the trip
notes: Off-season permits (Sep 28 - May 21) are free, self-issue, and available 24 hours at kiosks near each trailhead. Walk-up permits with no advance reservation are available from 1pm the day before entry, same fee, paid at the station. Rae Lakes Loop, High Sierra Trail and Copper Creek sell out fast on release day.
interagency_note: Confirmed and broadened: 'you can generally obtain your permit for your entire itinerary from the agency where your trip begins (e.g. the Inyo, Sierra, or Sequoia national forests, or Yosemite National Park)' -- reciprocity applies to Sierra NF and Yosemite NP too, not just Inyo NF as previously noted (still applies at the shared cross-Sierra passes: Taboose, Sawmill, Baxter, Shepherd Pass, Kearsarge Pass, Cottonwood Pass). OPEN QUESTION, not yet resolved: the source specifically flags that entries via Jennie Lakes Wilderness (Sequoia NF) DO need a SEKI recreation.gov permit if the route continues into the park, via the JO Pass, Belle Canyon, or Sugarloaf entry points -- even though Jennie Lakes Wilderness itself needs no permit for use that stays within it (see the 'none' permit_group note on the Marvin Pass trailhead). Whether the SPS peaks reached from Marvin Pass (Whaleback, Glacier Ridge) actually cross into SEKI via one of those three named entry points hasn't been confirmed -- don't assume 'none' is correct for that trailhead without checking.

permit_type: Golden Trout / Monarch / South Sierra Wilderness Permit (free, self-issue)
reservation_method: Confirmed via official page: "Visitor permits (required only for overnight stays in the Golden Trout Wilderness) are available from forest offices near wilderness entry points." Day use needs no wilderness permit.
notes: The source's wording is 'available from forest offices near wilderness entry points'. It does not say 'free' or 'self-issue', so the self-issue framing here follows the general USFS pattern for non-quota wildernesses rather than this page; whether the offices are staffed or unstaffed kiosks is not nailed down. The page's 'June-November' Seasons of Use is a snow-free access window, not a quota season -- the wilderness is confirmed non-quota. The wilderness spans both Sequoia and Inyo NF. Ranger district contacts: Kern River RD (760-376-3781); Western Divide RD, 32588 Highway 190, Springville CA 93265, (559-539-2607), Mon-Fri 8am-4:30pm.
excludes: Does NOT cover entries into the Golden Trout Wilderness via Cottonwood Basin or Cottonwood Pass. Those are issued by Inyo NF on a different, quota'd permit (permit_group inyo_gtw) with its own season, so a free Sequoia NF permit will not admit you there.

reservation_method: Reservable on recreation.gov up to 6 months before arrival. You select a Destination Zone (45 total, numbered 1-45) and must spend your FIRST night in it; after that you may move between zones on the same permit, provided you exit by the last date booked. The quota counts INDIVIDUALS selecting a zone for their first night, not permits or groups. The agency states it chose a destination-based quota rather than a trailhead-based one because Desolation is relatively small and many zones are reachable from a single trailhead. About two-thirds of each zone's quota is reservable online; the remaining ~one-third is held for same-day, first-come permits issued at a ranger station. In quota season the permit prints starting 7 days before entry; outside quota season it can be booked and printed on the day of entry, and no per-zone limit applies. Thru-hikers completing the full Tahoe Rim Trail loop in one continuous journey book a separate 'Tahoe Rim Trail (Thru Hike Only)' zone instead of a numbered one.
fee_notes: Overnight recreation fee is per ADULT (over 12): $5 for the 1st night, $10 for 2-14 nights. Children 12 and under are free. Capped at $100 of recreation fees per permit. A $6 non-refundable reservation fee applies to every overnight permit, on top of the recreation fee. A $20 Desolation annual pass makes the recreation fee free for the pass holder, but the $6/permit reservation fee still applies. America the Beautiful interagency passes (including Senior and Access) do NOT apply to this permit. Changing party size, number of days, or the first-night zone costs a $5 change fee; changing the entry date means cancelling and rebooking at another $6. Day-use permits are free. Pyramid Creek, Eagle Falls, Loon Lake, Rockbound, and Twin Lakes day use areas charge a parking fee, waived for overnight permit holders, who must display the parking pass in the vehicle.
notes: A signed, PRINTED permit must be carried by the group leader at all times -- a digital or paper reservation CONFIRMATION is not a valid permit. CANCELLATION: cancel 8 or more days before entry for a full refund of recreation fees; within 7 days nothing is refunded, and a no-show refunds nothing, so cancel to release quota for others. CHANGES are only allowed more than 8 days before entry -- once the permit becomes printable at 7 days out, no changes are possible. A free day-use permit is required ONLY during quota season, self-issued at a trailhead or obtained from a local Forest Service office; outside those dates Eldorado NF states plainly that none is needed, while recreation.gov's overview paragraph says year-round and contradicts its own operational section (reasoning at desolation-2026-09-12-13, closed at desolation-2026-09-12-11). CONDITIONS: the Caldor Fire burn scar holds dead and fire-weakened trees; heavy snow may begin in October and last through July, and most trailheads are not vehicle-accessible in winter. ACCESS GAP: the permit page names 13 trailheads -- Loon Lake, Van Vleck, Rockbound, Twin Lakes, Lyons Creek, Pyramid Creek, Ralston Peak, Echo Lake, Glen Alpine, Mt. Tallac, Bayview, Eagle Lake, Meeks Bay -- and this project holds three of them. The other ten are a known coverage gap, not a claim they do not exist.

reservation_method: Not reservable in advance — issued in person at the Carson Pass Information Station on the day of entry, first-come first-served (station only staffed in summer). Outside that window (roughly Sep 8 - May 30), the station is closed and permits are instead obtained in person at the Amador Ranger District office (26820 Silver Drive, Pioneer CA, Mon-Fri 8am-4:30pm) or by emailing SM.FS.mowilderness@usda.gov with name, phone, party size and destination the week of your trip -- this is NOT a self-issue kiosk system like the free permit groups.
fee_notes: No fee for the wilderness permit itself. PARKING, June 1 - October 31, at USFS-operated lots: $5.00 per day at Carson Pass, Carson Pass Overflow and Meiss trailheads, paid at a self-service iron ranger -- fill in the slip, put cash or a check in it, and display the tag on your dashboard; each day must be paid in full. Woods Lake trailhead is concession-operated and charges $8. America the Beautiful Senior and Access passes ARE accepted at the USFS lots (unlike on the Desolation overnight permit, where they are explicitly excluded). Whether a $20 season day-use pass still exists is an open conflict between two 2025 Forest Service documents -- see permit_source_log.csv. WINTER: a California State Parks Sno-Park permit is required instead, November 1 - May 31 (https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=30969).
notes: Only 14 CPMA camping permits per day in peak season (Memorial Day - Labor Day), max 8 people per permit, at 14 designated sites: 3 at Winnemucca Lake (2-night limit), 5 at Round Top Lake (2-night limit), 6 at Fourth of July Lake (3-night limit). Woods Lake and Frog Lake are day-use only, despite Frog Lake sitting inside the CPMA. Permits are issued from 8:00 AM on the day of entry and typically go within moments, so carry a backup plan outside the CPMA. Each site has a numbered wooden post and your permit is valid only at the site number it names. WINTER: with at least a foot of snow down, snow camping is not confined to the assigned sites, but a permit is still required and the water setbacks still apply. The agency calls this unit the Carson Pass Management AREA (CPMA) on its permit page and the Carson Pass Management UNIT (CPMU) in its FAQ; searching one term misses pages using the other. The 13-vs-14 designated site count is an open conflict: the 2025 instructions say 13 while their own breakdown sums to 14, and 14 is carried here.
excludes: Valid ONLY inside the Carson Pass Management Area, and only at the numbered site your permit names. It does not cover the wider Mokelumne Wilderness -- use the free general self-issue permit (permit_group mokelumne_free) for that.

reservation_method: Self-issue, but not a simple trailhead kiosk: EITHER download and fill out the General Mokelumne Wilderness permit form yourself, then print/sign/scan (or photo) and email it to SM.FS.mowilderness@usda.gov, OR go in person to the Amador Ranger District office (Silver Drive, Pioneer CA), open Tue-Sat 8am-4:30pm until September, closed federal holidays. This specific permit does NOT cover camping in the Carson Pass Management Area or its three lakes (Winnemucca/Round Top/Fourth of July) -- see the cpma group for that.
fee_notes: Free -- confirmed no quota or fee
notes: One permit per group, which must stay with a member of the party at all times; each permit is good for one trip only; you must enter at the trailhead named on the permit; and the signed permit must be carried on your person, not merely emailed. PARKING: no fee at the three most common non-CPMA entry points -- Salt Springs, the Bear River area (Tanglefoot trailhead) and the Silver Lake area (Allen Camp trailhead); most other Eldorado NF trailheads do charge. DAY USE: no permit is needed for day hiking anywhere in the Mokelumne, in either season -- unlike Desolation next door, which requires one at the trailhead during quota season. A day hike does not let you stay overnight.
excludes: Does NOT cover camping in the Carson Pass Management Area or its three lakes -- Winnemucca, Round Top and Fourth of July -- nor the trail from the Woods Lake / Carson Pass trailhead to them. That needs the quota'd CPMA permit (permit_group cpma), issued in person on the day of entry. Carrying the wrong one means you may not camp there at all.

reservation_method: In person during office hours at Sugar Pine Ranger Station (Hwy 108, Summit Ranger District -- covers Sonora Pass) or Calaveras Ranger Station (Hwy 4) / Lake Alpine Ranger Station, OR self-issue at the kiosk outside those stations when closed. Groveland Ranger Station (Hwy 120) issues by phone or in person, but ONLY 24 hours in advance (up to 3 days for holiday weekends) -- call 209-962-7825. Long-distance trips exiting toward Tuolumne Meadows or Echo Summit CANNOT use self-issue kiosks at all -- must call/visit a station in person; permits can be phoned in and mailed/emailed up to 7 days ahead.
notes: No quota or reservation system for Emigrant, Carson-Iceberg, or Stanislaus's portion of Mokelumne. Ebbetts Pass (Hwy 4) is within Humboldt-Toiyabe NF jurisdiction, not Stanislaus, and is tagged to the toiyabe_free group. Sonora Pass is confirmed Stanislaus NF (Summit Ranger District / Sugar Pine Ranger Station).
interagency_note: CORRECTS AND SHARPENS the Yosemite Kibbie Lake/Lake Eleanor detail: quota is exactly 25 people/day via Shingle Springs (Kibbie Lake) trailhead and 10 people/day via Lake Eleanor trailhead (Yosemite NP's own quota, administered through Stanislaus). Must call the Groveland Ranger District 1 day ahead, recommended at 8:30am (permits go quickly); for a Sunday/Monday start, call Friday (office closed Sat/Sun/holidays). Group size limited to 15 (8 if cross-country). Bear canisters ARE required and dogs are NOT allowed once you cross into Yosemite wilderness (unlike the Stanislaus side). These Yosemite-side permits are free and required year-round; the Cherry Lake Dam gate access road is open April 15 - Dec 15. All Yosemite NP wilderness regulations apply once inside the park. No separate Yosemite permit needed for a single continuous trip that starts at a Stanislaus trailhead.

permit_type: Non-Hoover Wilderness Permit (Carson-Iceberg, e.g. Ebbetts Pass) -- free, self-issue (not independently confirmed, see notes)
reservation_method: NOT independently confirmed for this specific forest/wilderness combination -- inferred from the general USFS non-quota-wilderness pattern (matching inyo_hoover_nonquota, gtw_free, mokelumne_free, stanislaus_free) plus the Stanislaus NF permit page's cross-reference. Contact the Humboldt-Toiyabe NF Carson Ranger District directly before relying on this.
notes: LOWER CONFIDENCE THAN THE OTHER GROUPS. Stanislaus NF's own wilderness-permits page states that Ebbetts Pass is within the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest boundary and directs visitors there for a long-distance permit from that trailhead. This row is built from that cross-reference plus the general non-quota-wilderness pattern, NOT from Humboldt-Toiyabe's own site -- check against fs.usda.gov/r04/humboldt-toiyabe before relying on it.
